quotes.text: The road from Stellenbosch to Malmesbury crosses the national road from Cape Town to Paarl by an overhead bridge about 40 kilometres from Cape Town. Not far away, in the northern angle of these two roads, amongst some trees, stands the old Cape Dutch house Type of site: Farm Complex. A particularly fine Old Cape farmhouse. The front gable bears the date 1756. It is, as far as is known, the oldest Old Cape gable still in existence and probably the only remaining gable of its type.

measurements.as_printed: The front gable bears the date 1756
measurements.note: A YEAR, not a dimension, and carried with NO `value` and NO `unit` for the same reason as Morgenster's. It is here because the register attaches a superlative to it -- the oldest surviving Old Cape gable -- and a dated fabric element is the only hard chronology this cluster's sources supply.

note: Tranche 3, Cape cluster, 5 September 2026. Added by this tranche as the earliest DATED gable the register knows of: 'It is, as far as is known, the oldest Old Cape gable still in existence and probably the only remaining gable of its type.' The superlative is the register's own and is quoted rather than restated, with its own two hedges ('as far as is known', 'probably') intact -- which is the difference between a standing this corpus may assert and one it may only report.
